title: Two processes, two page tables, one memory chip
desc: A drawing of two app processes using the same virtual address, each translated through its own page table by the memory management unit, landing on different physical pages.

steps.note: Your app holds an object at an address. That number is not a place in memory.
On every access the MMU translates it, using the page table the kernel keeps for your process.
The table says which physical page that is. Your code never learns the answer.
Another app has its own address space and its own table, written by the same kernel.
The very same virtual address, translated through that table, lands somewhere else entirely.
Your table has no entry reaching its pages. There is no number you could use. That is isolation.
